playbookOutputs: CIPC confirmation that the company status is restored to 'In Business'
Filed outstanding annual returns and certificates
Signed CoR40.5 application and supporting affidavit (client copy)
playbookCommonFailures: Company is only in 'AR Deregistration' (process), not final — it needs annual returns filed, not a CoR40.5
Affidavit does not explain why the company was in business at deregistration and why reinstatement is needed
Deed search not obtained, or company owns immovable property so extra documents are needed
Certified director ID older than 3 months
Outstanding annual return fees and penalties not paid after reinstatement, so the company drops back into deregistration

informationToProvide.label: Company Registration Certificate (CoR 14.3 / CK1)
informationToProvide.helpText: Upload the original CIPC registration certificate or latest disclosure document.
informationToProvide.aiHint: Official CIPC CoR14.3, CK1, CK2 or Disclosure Certificate showing the deregistered enterprise name, registration number, and listed directors/members.

informationToProvide.label: Certified SA ID Copies of All Directors / Members (Not Older Than 3 Months)
alternatives: Certified & apostilled foreign passport (foreign directors only)
informationToProvide.helpText: CIPC strictly requires clearly legible certified ID copies (< 3 months) for every director/member on record.
informationToProvide.aiHint: Mandatory CIPC KYC Invariant: South African citizens MUST submit a certified SA ID (Smart ID Card front AND back, or Green Barcoded ID Book) certified within the last 3 months by a Commissioner of Oaths or SAPS — passports are NOT accepted for SA citizens. Foreign nationals ONLY may submit a certified/apostilled foreign passport accompanied by a valid visa/permit. Verify legible ID/passport number, full legal names, and certification stamp date within 90 days.

informationToProvide.label: Documentary Proof of Active Trading OR Economic Value at Date of Deregistration (Bank Statement, Lease, Invoices, or Property Deed)
alternatives: Title deed of property in company name
Signed lease agreement or customer/supplier invoices at deregistration date
informationToProvide.helpText: Per CIPC Practice Note on CoR 40.5, upload proof that the company was in business OR held assets/liabilities at the date of deregistration.
informationToProvide.aiHint: Bank statement, property title deed, lease agreement, or customer/supplier invoices in the name of the deregistered entity showing activity, assets, or liabilities at the time of deregistration.

informationToProvide.label: Multiple Deeds Office Search Report Across All 10 Regional Deeds Offices
informationToProvide.helpText: Upload the Multiple Deeds Search report across all 10 regional Deeds Offices confirming whether the company owns immovable property.
informationToProvide.aiHint: Deeds Office search report (LexisNexis / WinDeed / SearchWorks) covering South African regional Deeds Offices showing whether immovable property is registered in the enterprise name.

informationToProvide.label: Dept of Public Works & National Treasury Non-Objection Letters (Required ONLY if Company Owns Immovable Property)
informationToProvide.conditionalQuestion: Does the company own any immovable property (land or buildings) registered at the Deeds Office?
informationToProvide.helpText: If the company owns immovable property, CIPC requires formal letters from the Department of Public Works and National Treasury confirming no bona vacantia objection.
informationToProvide.aiHint: Official letters from the Department of Public Works and National Treasury referencing the enterprise name and registration number and confirming no objection to CoR 40.5 reinstatement.

informationToProvide.label: Reason Annual Returns Were Not Filed & Annual Turnover for Each Outstanding Year
informationToProvide.helpText: Provide a brief explanation of why the company was deregistered (for the Sworn Affidavit) and list the annual turnover for each outstanding financial year.

informationToProvide.label: Signed CoR 40.5 Application, Sworn Affidavit (Commissioner of Oaths) & Mandate
informationToProvide.helpText: Once we draft the CoR 40.5 form, Sworn Affidavit, and Mandate, have the director sign and commission the affidavit before a Commissioner of Oaths and upload the single merged PDF pack.
informationToProvide.aiHint: Signed CIPC CoR 40.5 reinstatement form, signed Mandate/POA on company letterhead, and Sworn Affidavit commissioned by a Commissioner of Oaths with visible stamp and date.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Collect company documents, director IDs and reason for reinstatement
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: CoR14.3, certified IDs for all directors, reason, nature of business and turnover per outstanding year received
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: Explain that the R200 CIPC reinstatement fee and the outstanding annual return fees and penalties are payable in addition to our R700 and will be shown as disbursements. Ask whether the company owns immovable property or has any assets — this determines the supporting documents. Ask whether the company was trading on the date it was deregistered (it must have been, or be able to show a real reason to be restored).

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Assess deregistration status and reinstatement route
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: CIPC status recorded; route decided: file outstanding ARs only (status 'AR Deregistration') or full CoR40.5 reinstatement (status 'Final Deregistration')
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: Check the enterprise status on CIPC e-Services. If status is 'AR Deregistration' (deregistration in process), no CoR40.5 is needed — filing all outstanding annual returns restores it; skip to re_file_ar. If 'Final Deregistration' / 'Deregistered', the full reinstatement applies. ⚠ verify the current CIPC supporting-document list for CoR40.5; understood to be: certified ID of the applicant and of a director, a deed search (Deeds Office) confirming whether the company owns property, an affidavit explaining why the company was deregistered and the reason for reinstatement, and proof of trading at deregistration (e.g. bank statement, contract). Some CIPC practice notes have also required letters from the Deeds Office / Treasury where property is held — flag for Kevin.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Draft CoR40.5 handoff sheet, affidavit text and cover letter
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: CoR40.5 fields, affidavit wording and cover letter drafted for Kevin's review
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: The affidavit (sworn by a director before a Commissioner of Oaths) must state: the company's name and number, that it was in business / owns assets on the deregistration date, the reason for the failure to file annual returns, and why reinstatement is required. Do not invent facts — use the client's stated reason verbatim and flag gaps. The cover letter lists all attachments. The resolution records the board's decision to apply for reinstatement.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Send CoR40.5 and affidavit for signature and commissioning
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: Signed CoR40.5, commissioned affidavit and resolution uploaded
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: Explain that the affidavit must be signed in front of a Commissioner of Oaths (any police station, attorney or bank branch offers this free). Return everything as PDF.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: File CoR40.5 reinstatement application on CIPC
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: Reinstatement application submitted with all supporting documents; R200 fee paid; tracking number saved
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: Kevin files — professional judgement on the supporting pack and the fee is money. CIPC e-Services > Transact > Re-instatement (CoR40.5). Upload the signed form, affidavit, certified IDs, deed search, proof of trading and cover letter. Confirm the customer account holds the R200 fee. Record the tracking number.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Wait for CIPC reinstatement decision
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: CIPC confirms reinstatement or issues a query
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: The catalogue turnaround is 1-2 working days after everything is in hand, but CIPC reinstatements frequently take longer — check tracking status before each follow-up and keep the client informed without promising a date. Quote any query to Kevin verbatim.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: File all outstanding annual returns
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: Every outstanding annual return filed and fees/penalties paid; status 'In Business'
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: Once reinstated (or immediately if the status was only 'AR Deregistration'), file the outstanding years oldest first with the turnover per year. Beneficial ownership declaration may be required first — check and propose that service if missing. Confirm the customer account balance covers the total before submitting.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Deliver reinstatement confirmation and annual return certificates
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: Status printout, AR certificates and re-downloaded CoR14.3 posted to Communication History
fulfillmentChecklist.aiInstructions: State the next annual return date and note the disbursements (R200 fee plus AR fees) for invoicing. Offer an annual return reminder.

fulfillmentChecklist.title: Final sign-off
fulfillmentChecklist.doneCriteria: Kevin confirms the order can be completed
